_note: THE ONE FIXTURE OF MALFORMED LADDER FAMILIES. Every implementation of the type-ladder derivation is driven against THESE cases and no others, so the four ways a ladder can go blind are stated once. Read design/ladder-refusal-conformance.test.mjs for the roster, the drivers and why the three implementations are NOT shared.
_contract: A malformed family must REFUSE — throw, or return an { err } carrying the sentinel, or exit non-zero naming it. Returning [] or a partial list is the defect: every downstream ladder assertion then passes vacuously.

implementations.refuses_by: return { err }, collected into the numbered problem report, non-zero exit

implementations.driven_by: web/__tests__/type-ladder-emitted.test.ts itself — the doc-gates design job runs Node 20, which cannot execute TypeScript, so the web arm is driven where TypeScript already runs. Same fixture, different runner.

cases.why: type.chrome absent entirely — the derivation has nothing to read and must not hand back []
type.chrome is a scalar — Object.entries(7) is [] and every assertion downstream passes vacuously
an object with no entry carrying a finite positive size — the ladder derives to nothing
two rungs of the same size do not name ONE order, so neither 'largest to smallest' nor its reverse is defined
